minutes.headline: Sewer Commission backed extra paid hours to load meter IDs and approved the updated deduct meter policy.
minutes.summary: The commission, meeting remotely, reviewed the operations and maintenance RFP schedule, approved updates to the irrigation deduct meter policy, and heard about the Bright Farms project. It discussed a protocol for contacting town counsel and a request from the town's consultant about the meter ID import project. It agreed informally to support extra hours for help, pending the town manager's approval.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept the updated irrigation deduct meter policy and credit program, dated 7/28/2020.
Members agreed informally that the business manager will write the town manager to endorse about 50 extra hours of help entering meter IDs, subject to the town manager's approval.
Members agreed on a protocol: the business manager is the point person for town counsel, and commissioners inform each other before seeing counsel.
The commission heard that the FY21 budget report is not final because FY20 encumbered purchase orders are on hold and some invoices cannot yet be processed.
The operations and maintenance RFP for the stations was circulated, with a bid deadline and award date set.

why_it_matters: The deduct meter policy decides how irrigation-meter customers get credit on their sewer bills, and the commission said it will be posted and brought back for public approval.
The extra paid hours and the Woodard & Curran billing work bear on whether meter data is loaded correctly, which feeds the sewer bills residents receive.
watch_next: Meetings are set for Aug 11 and Aug 25, 2020.
The business manager is to send the Woodard & Curran scope of services to members before the next meeting, and the updated deduct meter policy is to be posted and brought back for public approval.
